paper_title: An STM study of molecular exchange processes in organic thin film growth

knowledge_points.content: The molecular exchange process between PCBM and exTTF at the monolayer level is primarily driven by the higher adsorption energy of PCBM on Au(111) compared to exTTF.
knowledge_points.evidence: The place exchange at the level of the monolayer is driven by the difference in the interaction with the Au(111) substrate; while the adsorption energy of exTTF on Au(111) is only of 0.32 eV per molecule, the expected adsorption energy of PCBM is substantially larger, since for C60 on Au(111) it is of the order of 1.9 eV per molecule.

knowledge_points.content: Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) at 150 K reveals that PCBM molecules initially deposited on top of an exTTF monolayer eventually embed themselves into the first layer, displacing exTTF molecules to the second layer.
knowledge_points.evidence: We thus conclude that PCBM molecules initially on top of the exTTF layer are now in direct contact with the Au(111) surface in the first layer, while some exTTF molecules have been displaced from the first to the second layer.

knowledge_points.content: A vertical superlattice of exTTF and PCBM is difficult to achieve at the monolayer level because PCBM spontaneously exchanges places with exTTF to bind directly to the gold substrate.
knowledge_points.evidence: In an attempt to build an exTTF–PCBM vertical superlattice, we deposited PCBM on top of a complete monolayer of exTTF... PCBM molecules have exchanged places with the exTTF molecules underneath, which have, in turn, diffused over the surface to form the characteristic second layer rows.

knowledge_points.content: When PCBM is deposited on a thick exTTF film (approximately 2.5 ML), the exchange process is inhibited, and PCBM grows via the Volmer–Weber (3D island) mechanism due to high surface free energy.
knowledge_points.evidence: When grown on 1 ML of exTTF, the PCBM molecules can exchange places with the exTTF molecules to bind strongly to Au(111), but 2 ML of exTTF already constitute a barrier large enough to prevent the diffusion of PCBM to the gold layer... and 3D island growth takes over.

knowledge_points.content: The adsorption energy of PCBM on Au(111) is approximately 1.9 eV per molecule, while the adsorption energy of exTTF on the same substrate is approximately 0.32 eV per molecule.
knowledge_points.evidence: the adsorption energy of exTTF on Au(111) is only of 0.32 eV per molecule... for C60 on Au(111) it is of the order of 1.9 eV per molecule.

knowledge_points.content: PCBM and exTTF do not form mixed 2D crystalline phases on Au(111) because they are structurally unequivalent and their distinct shapes (spherical vs. planar derivative) disfavor intermixing.
knowledge_points.evidence: PCBM and exTTF do not mix on the gold surface (as shown in Fig. 1d), one of the reasons probably being that they are shape and structurally unequivalent, a condition that disfavours intermixing.

knowledge_points.content: Sequential deposition of PCBM and exTTF on Au(111) at coverages below one monolayer results in a lateral superlattice of interdigitated nanoscale stripes with widths of 10–20 nm.
knowledge_points.evidence: The resulting morphology, a lateral superlattice of interdigitated nanoscale stripes with a characteristic width of about 10-20 nm, has been predicted to optimize the efficiency of bulk-heterojunction organic solar cells.

knowledge_points.content: The separation between exTTF molecules along their characteristic 1D rows in the second layer is 7.7 Å, which is significantly smaller than the minimum van der Waals separation of 10 Å required for PCBM molecules.
knowledge_points.evidence: the separation between molecules along the rows is 7.7 Å (as in C60 the minimum separation between two PCBM molecules is 10 Å).

knowledge_points.content: The cohesive energy of PCBM is approximately 1.3 eV, which is higher than that of the parent TTF compound (approximately 1.1 eV), contributing to the tendency of PCBM to form 3D clusters when not in contact with the gold substrate.
knowledge_points.evidence: the observation of 3D growth of PCBM on exTTF is in agreement with values for the cohesive energy of PCBM (1.3 eV) and of the parent compound TTF (~1.1 eV).

knowledge_points.content: At 150 K, the exTTF layer on Au(111) is effectively frozen, as evidenced by the lack of displacement in naturally occurring vacancies during sequential STM imaging.
knowledge_points.evidence: At this temperature [150 K], the exTTF layer is almost completely frozen, as evidenced by the sequence imaging of the same area of the sample: the naturally occurring vacancies present in the exTTF layer... do not show any displacement from one image to the next.
